chapter: Swing, singers, Ed Fox and recordings
title: The 1937 shake-up and men from Horace Henderson's band
summary: Hines wanted a new band; the style changed.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Well, let's go back to that 1937 shake-up. Since there were only three of you carried over, it seems like that was a major change in the Hines' band. And as far as I can tell, I haven't seen anything that Earl has talked about it. I'm just very, very curious. Did Earl want a new band?
It seemed like he wanted a new band.
I mean, was there some dissension in the band?

No, there wasn't any dissension or nothing. I don't -- it was a strange thing. Well, you know, if the leader wants to change the complexion of his band, there's nothing you can do about that. So I guess that's what he wanted to do.
How did that effect the music?
Because Budd left, who was doing a lot of the arrangements you said.
Uh-huh. That's when Willy Randall came in the band.
Yeah, Willy Randall came. Did Willy start doing a lot of arrangements?
Yeah, he did a lot of arranging, too.
How did it change the band?
It changed the style of the band.

Well, it's hard to say, because we had -- when we made that major change like that, most of the men coming into the band, as I say, was from Horace Henderson's band. And they had a different style than we had. So we adapted our style.
Well, did Earl hear these guys? Did Horace play the Grand Terrace?
No, he was at the Rum Boogie. Then when he left the Rum Boogie, the men was available. So he saw -- I guess Earl got the idea.
That's when Horace went to New York?
